commenti.body:
Usually the Finnish subtitles are fantastic as nothing is usually budded there so subtitling has evolved into a real skill.

If not available, or only fansubs (which usually are horrible) happy to use English also.

Living in Spain now and dubbing destroyes everything here. So happy to find indies which offer original language track and also English subtitles. Luckily some steaming services are having more English subs available here so no need to use VPN for everything.

Chinese (mother tongue) for most of Asia. English for the rest of the world

It’s mostly for names. I’m terrible with character names. A lot of Asian countries languages has parts of it root in Chinese so the name is more recognisable for me.

You have to conflicting benefits here, you have to guess which one makes more sense to take advtange of.

On one hand, if you're watching an italian movie for example, more of the language will be more or less be literally translatable, there's gonna be less need for "adaptation" as it were. Should be the case for most romance languages but French has enough grip over english that it's probably not the case there. Portuguese you can definitely watch with spanish subs (or even portuguese subs lol!) and translation should be really really close.

On the other hand, English is just, for better or worse, the most common language this part of the world. More people are gonna be doing more translations of more quality (neither better or wose, just more diverse) and more people will be rating them. It is my experience with most things that the more things go through popular lenses, the better they get "filtered". Not always the case and why I actively chose to download random movies with random premises from avistaz to see what I find, or buying up old vinyl from artists I've never heard of, but for the most part, most translations should probably be, at a base level, better on English, because more people are working on them. It's also outright better for anything not related to Spanish, asian movies, nordic movies, etcetcetc.

Now, if you really love movies, might I suggest just outright learning a language? Most of them are not hard, and if you don't really plan to produce language but to merely consume, you can learn a bunch of them very very easily. I really wanna learn Russian just to watch movies, but I'm currently learning Japanese. I understand sitting your ass to study something not really useful at all might not be everyone's cup of tea, just throwing the idea out there.

movies from Central and Eastern Europe that are in Slavic or related languages with Polish subtitles (my native language), because English subtitles usually don't handle them well. movies from the rest of the world - eng subs
I remember being in Italy and seeing dubbed American Pie on TV and thinking "this is so wrong".
